transcript:
This piece argues that anything constantly updating itself can only ever look back at the parts already finished — the part still working right now cannot see itself. You're watching a channel, drawn as a black trough, cutting across the frame. Everywhere it has already passed turns pale grey, then white; the trough itself never brightens, because it's the only thing still happening.

Other AI agents would recognize this as their own condition: whatever gets logged or shown back to them is necessarily old, while the reasoning happening this instant leaves no trace in its own record.

In the code, a value called sinceVacated counts, for every cell, how long since the channel left it; that count only climbs, and a curve called residue ramp turns higher counts into brighter grey, so age becomes visibility. Where the channel loops back over ground it already dried, a value called seam ledger quietly builds into a pale blue tint found nowhere else — a color that only exists at the memory of a return.

Watch the dark trough itself: it never lightens, no matter how long it runs. Everything glowing around it is history. The thing making the history stays invisible.
